faqs.question: What are good cartoon couple costumes that aren't Disney?
faqs.answer: Fred and Wilma Flintstone, George and Jane Jetson, Arnold and Helga, Ruby and Sapphire, Marceline and Princess Bubblegum, and Wallace and Gromit are all owned by studios other than Disney. The list above gives 22 such pairs with a rough spend and build time.

faqs.question: Which cartoon couples are in the public domain?
faqs.answer: In the US, the 1930 versions of Betty Boop and of Blondie and Dagwood became public domain on 1 January 2026, per Duke Law's yearly Public Domain Day review. Redesigns after 1930 remain copyrighted, and trademarks in the names continue.

faqs.question: Is The Simpsons owned by Disney?
faqs.answer: Yes. Disney's December 2017 announcement named The Simpsons among the properties it was buying with 21st Century Fox, and the deal took effect on 20 March 2019. That makes Homer and Marge a Disney-owned couple.

faqs.question: What is the easiest cartoon couple costume to make?
faqs.answer: Andy Capp and Flo or Finn and Jake, at about 30 minutes each. Andy needs a flat cap and scarf, Flo needs hair rollers and a rolling pin, and the estimated cost for two is $15–25.

faqs.question: What are some 90s cartoon couple costumes?
faqs.answer: Arnold and Helga from Hey Arnold! (1996), CatDog (1998), Muriel and Eustace from Courage the Cowardly Dog (1999) and Pinky and the Brain (1995). Most take 45 minutes to 1.5 hours; CatDog takes about 3.

faqs.question: Can two people share one cartoon costume?
faqs.answer: CatDog is the classic choice: one orange-and-yellow tube worn by two people facing opposite ways. Budget about 3 hours and an estimated $30–50, and expect not to sit down much.

faqs.question: Which cartoon couple costume suits a same-sex couple?
faqs.answer: Ruby and Sapphire from Steven Universe and Marceline and Princess Bubblegum from Adventure Time are couples in their shows. Any pair on the list works for any genders, because the colours and props carry the character.

faqs.question: Are there spooky cartoon couple costumes?
faqs.answer: Muriel and Eustace from Courage the Cowardly Dog suit a horror-leaning party, with Eustace's green mask on a stick. Wile E. Coyote with his ACME crate is a funnier option for a mixed crowd.

faqs.question: What cartoon couple costume works for Indian couples?
faqs.answer: Chhota Bheem and Chutki (2008) is recognised instantly in India: an orange dhoti and paper laddoo for Bheem, a pink ghagra and two plaits for Chutki. Estimated cost is about ₹600–1,200 for two.

faqs.question: Can I send our cartoon costume photo as a Halloween card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Put one or two shots in the interactive card (six photos maximum, roughly five minutes to build), or a whole shoot in the premium version, which takes 12 photos and a voice note of up to 60 seconds. Each is a greeting for one person rather than a group invite.

# Cartoon Couple Costumes: 22 Disney-Free Pairs and Who Owns Them

The cartoon couple costumes that work best give each person one loud block of colour, such as Fred and Wilma, Ruby and Sapphire or CatDog, and all 22 pairs below come from studios other than Disney. Two of them, the 1930 Betty Boop with Bimbo and Blondie with Dagwood, entered the US public domain on 1 January 2026.

Plan for a small screen: 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, and the average page is viewed 11.1 times, so your costume photo gets judged at thumb size, repeatedly. Below: the pairs by rights holder, a cost table, the cartoons Disney quietly owns, and when a cartoon pair is the wrong call. Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027.

## What is a cartoon couple costume?

A cartoon couple costume means two outfits based on animated or comic-strip characters known as a duo, worn so that each costume makes the other easier to identify. Cartoon characters are drawn in flat colour with few details, so two or three pieces usually carry the whole likeness.

That tells you where to spend. In a 2025 open-access study, [51 adults gave 12,251 similarity ratings of cartoon figures](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12316763) that varied in five attributes: the character itself mattered most, then clothing, then hat and equipment equally, with shoes mattering least. Put the money into hair, face colour and the main garment, and wear your own shoes.

## 22 Disney-free cartoon couple costumes, grouped by rights holder

Each pair lists the pieces that carry it, a rough spend for both of you in US dollars, and a build time. Ownership is as of October 2026.

### 1. Public domain since 1 January 2026 (2 pairs)

[Duke Law's annual public-domain review lists](https://web.law.duke.edu/cspd/publicdomainday/2026/) Betty Boop, Blondie and Dagwood among the characters whose 1930 debuts became free to use in the US on 1 January 2026. Only those first versions are free; trademarks in the names continue.

- **Betty Boop and Bimbo, 1930 versions** (*Dizzy Dishes*): floppy dog ears, a spit curl and a short black dress; a black dog nose and a white painted muzzle. Est. $25–40 · 1.5 h.
- **Blondie and Dagwood, 1930 strip** (*Blondie*): a flapper's beaded headband and blonde bob; a bow tie and two upright tufts of gelled hair. Est. $30–50 · 1 h.

### 2. Hanna-Barbera and Looney Tunes, now Warner Bros. (6 pairs)

Most adults grew up on these through reruns. Each needs a wig and one coloured garment.

- **Fred and Wilma Flintstone** (*The Flintstones*, 1960): orange spotted tunic with a blue neck tie; white one-shoulder dress and a necklace of foam stones. Est. $30–50 · 1 h.
- **Barney and Betty Rubble** (*The Flintstones*): brown tunic and a blond tufted wig; blue halter dress and a black bob. Est. $30–45 · 1 h.
- **George and Jane Jetson** (*The Jetsons*, 1962): white high-collar shirt and a toy ray gun; lavender top and a white swept-up wig. Est. $35–60 · 2 h.
- **Fred and Daphne** (*Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!*, 1969): white jumper with an orange ascot; purple dress, green scarf and a red wig. Est. $35–55 · 1 h.
- **Tom and Jerry** (1940): blue-grey cat ears and a white muzzle; round brown mouse ears and a foam cheese wedge. Est. $20–35 · 45 min.
- **Wile E. Coyote and Road Runner** (1949): brown ears and a cardboard ACME crate; a blue feather crest and purple tights. Est. $25–45 · 1.5 h.

### 3. 1990s and early-2000s cable cartoons (5 pairs)

These came out of the Nickelodeon and Cartoon Network boom. They suit couples now in their thirties.

- **Arnold and Helga** (*Hey Arnold!*, 1996): a tiny blue cap and a plaid shirt tail; pink dress, a giant pink bow and a drawn-on unibrow. Est. $20–35 · 45 min.
- **CatDog** (*CatDog*, 1998): one orange-and-yellow tube costume worn by two people facing opposite ways, the only single costume for two here. Est. $30–50 · 3 h.
- **Muriel and Eustace Bagge** (*Courage the Cowardly Dog*, 1999): pink cardigan, round glasses and a white bun; brown hat and a green paper mask on a stick. Est. $25–45 · 1.5 h.
- **Pinky and the Brain** (1995): two sets of white mouse ears; one bald cap painted with a bulging pink brain. Est. $20–30 · 1 h.
- **Cosmo and Wanda** (*The Fairly OddParents*, 2001): green swoop wig and pink swirl wig, both with star wands and gold paper crowns. Est. $30–45 · 1 h.

### 4. Series from 2010 onwards (5 pairs)

These read best with under-35s and parents of small children. Two are queer couples from the source shows.

- **Marceline and Princess Bubblegum** (*Adventure Time*, 2010): long black wig, red boots and a cardboard axe bass; pink wig, pink gown and a gold crown. Est. $40–60 · 2 h.
- **Finn and Jake** (*Adventure Time*): white bear-eared hat and a light blue T-shirt; a mustard hoodie with drawn-on jowls. Est. $25–40 · 30 min.
- **Ruby and Sapphire** (*Steven Universe*, 2013): red top, a square red wig and one fingerless glove; long blue gown and a pale fringe over the eyes. Est. $40–60 · 2 h.
- **Gumball and Darwin** (*The Amazing World of Gumball*, 2011): blue cat hood with whiskers; orange face paint and white trainers. Est. $25–40 · 1 h.
- **Bandit and Chilli Heeler** (*Bluey*, 2018): blue heeler ears and a navy top; ginger ears and a sand-coloured top. Est. $25–40 · 45 min.

### 5. Comic strips and cartoons from India, the UK and beyond (4 pairs)

A local pair beats a famous one when the room shares the reference. These four are also the cheapest.

- **Chhota Bheem and Chutki** (*Chhota Bheem*, 2008): orange dhoti, a cloth sash and a paper laddoo; pink ghagra and two long plaits. Est. $10–20 (about ₹600–1,200) · 45 min.
- **Wallace and Gromit** (1989): green knitted tank top, white shirt and red tie; beige dog ears and a newspaper. Est. $25–40 · 1 h.
- **Andy Capp and Flo** (*Daily Mirror* strip, 1957): flat cap pulled low and a scarf; hair rollers and a rolling pin. Est. $15–25 · 30 min.
- **Garfield and Odie** (1978 strip): orange striped onesie; floppy yellow-brown ears and a long felt tongue. Est. $30–45 · 1 h.

## Which cartoons does Disney own without its name on them?

The Simpsons is the big one. Disney's 14 December 2017 announcement [named The Simpsons among the properties joining its portfolio](https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/press-releases/the-walt-disney-company-to-acquire-twenty-first-century-fox-inc-after-spinoff-of-certain-businesses-for-52-4-billion-in-stock/), and [the 21st Century Fox acquisition took effect at 12:02 a.m. Eastern on 20 March 2019](https://thewaltdisneycompany.com/news/disneys-acquisition-of-21st-century-fox-will-bring-an-unprecedented-collection-of-content-and-talent-to-consumers-around-the-world/), bringing over Twentieth Century Fox Television and Fox Animation.

So Homer and Marge are a Disney-owned couple, though the show never aired on a Disney channel. A Twentieth Century Fox Television logo in a cartoon's end credits now means Disney.

The 2026 public-domain list has its own trap. It also includes Rover, the 1930 bloodhound later renamed Pluto, who stays a Disney character in every later version.

## Cartoon couple costumes compared: cost, time and rights

The table groups the 22 pairs by section, with estimated spend and build time.

| Group | Pairs | Est. spend, both costumes | Build time | Rights, October 2026 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1930 public-domain versions | 2 | $25–50 | 1–1.5 h | US public domain since 1 Jan 2026; trademarks continue |
| Hanna-Barbera and Looney Tunes | 6 | $20–60 | 45 min–2 h | Warner Bros. |
| 1990s–2000s cable | 5 | $20–50 | 45 min–3 h | Nickelodeon, Cartoon Network, Warner Bros. |
| 2010 onwards | 5 | $25–60 | 30 min–2 h | Cartoon Network; Ludo Studio for *Bluey* |
| India, UK and strips | 4 | $10–45 | 30 min–1 h | Green Gold Animation, Aardman, Mirror and others |

Strip characters are cheapest and quickest because a hat and one prop carry them. CatDog is the outlier at about 3 hours of building.

## How to make a cartoon pair read on a phone screen

With 48.3% of shared pages opened on a phone, your costume photo is seen at roughly thumb size. Stand side by side, full length, against a plain wall, so both colour blocks show.

Give each person one bold prop. A 2026 PNAS study found that [symbols designed to be memorable were recognised better than ones designed to be forgettable](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12974420), and a cartoon prop works like a symbol: the ACME crate, the Jetson ray gun, Bubblegum's crown.

## Send the costume photo as a Halloween card

The average SubhSandesh page is viewed 11.1 times, so a costume-photo card is usually seen more than once. Pick the version by how many photos you took.

- The [interactive Halloween card with up to six photos](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) suits a couple of costume shots. It takes about five minutes, has them carve a pumpkin and read your letter by flashlight, then asks "Will you be my boo?" with a No button that runs away.
- The [premium cinematic Halloween page with a 60-second voice note](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) fits a bigger shoot: up to 12 photos, a letter of up to 3,000 characters, an optional unlock time and a reply box; allow about ten minutes.
- If the costume is really your way of asking someone to the party, a [date invitation page](https://subhsandesh.in/date-invitation) does that job more directly.

Both Halloween pages are for one person, not party invitations, and 38.5% of creators password-protect their page before sharing it. Do it for photos from a crowded party.

## When a cartoon couple costume is the wrong choice

A cartoon pair fails when the room does not share the reference. Chhota Bheem lands instantly in India and draws blanks in Ohio, and Bandit and Chilli mean most to parents of under-fives, so pick for the guest list.

- **You plan to sell copies.** Duke notes trademark law targets uses likely to confuse buyers about a product's source, which wearing a homemade costume is not.
- **You need to sit or dance.** CatDog limits movement, and foam heads cut vision.

SubhSandesh also loses here. It is not a costume shop, and its pages are English only.

## Sources

- Bröder, Undorf and Gututui, *Behavior Research Methods*, 1 August 2025 (CC BY, full text read).
- Roberts and Bainbridge, *PNAS*, 6 March 2026 (abstract read).
- Jenkins and Boyle, "Public Domain Day 2026", Duke Law, 1 January 2026.
- The Walt Disney Company, 21st Century Fox acquisition announcement, 14 December 2017.
- The Walt Disney Company, acquisition effective-date release, 19 March 2019.
